name: Підготовка наскрізної атаки: жертва
description:
In this lesson we look at sacrifice by capturing. In Example 1, we see how a sacrifice forces two enemy pieces in alignment. In Example 2, we look at the elimination of a defender.

What do you have to do?
Sacrifice a piece with a capture. Locate a head piece or eliminate a defender. Subsequently win material with a skewer.

examples.text: The black bishop on c6 and black rook are on the same diagonal. However, White cannot take immediate advantage of this. Against 1.Bb5, black plays 1...Bxb5. Better is to place a piece on c6: 1.Rxc6! If black does not capture the rook, white has simply won a bishop. If black does capture the rook (1...Kxc6), the king can be targeted. Now 2.Bb5+ is a lot better for white than it was a move ago. It is skewer! After 2...Kd6 3.Bxe8 white stays ahead a bishop.

examples.pgn: {[%csl Re6,Rg8][%cal Gc4g8] [#]} 1. Qxd4 $1 exd4 2. Bc4+ Ke5 3. Bxg8 *
examples.text: The black king (head piece) and queen (tail piece) are on the same diagonal. However, 1.Bc4+ is not useful, because black can capture the bishop (1...Rxc4). Eliminating the defender by capturing offers the solution: 1.Qxd4! exd4. White has sacrificed a queen for a rook, but now has a decisive  skewer with 2.Bc4+ Ke5 3.Bxg8. White has won a rook with this sequence!

puzzles.pgn: {[%csl Rd2,Rd3,Rd5][%cal Gd8d2] [#]} {Q=1} 1... Rxd5 ! 2. Qxd5 {Q=2} Rd8 3. Qf3 Rxd2 *
texts: Sometimes you can temporarily sacrifice material to regain it with interest.
